resources.string: None of the words you dictate stay on this phone
Once a dictation is in the field, Embersay forgets it: no Try again, no Last dictation, no Insert again, Copy last or Undo last, no history. A dictation that could not go in is gone.
Only how many characters and words a dictation had, and its language.
Each dictation\'s time, word count and length - no words, no app, nor how the text got into each app. Switch the statistics off on their page to keep none of it.
Embersay never puts text on it; using the clipboard when typing fails is off.
No screenshots or screen recordings of Embersay, and a blank picture in recent apps.
Switching it on deletes what is kept now: the last dictations, the history and the app names in the statistics.
Anyone with your phone can see that Embersay is installed.
What you dictated into a chat, a note or a mail stays there. Text copied before may stay in a keyboard\'s own clipboard history (Gboard, Samsung).
A speech recognition or cleanup on a server still receives your recording or its text. Only speech recognition on this phone, with the cleanup off, keeps it all here.
Not inserted - the security mode keeps no copy
May still show up - the security mode keeps no copy
Screen was off - not inserted, the security mode keeps no copy
On this phone, never in a backup: the words and the app encrypted, the time not.
Readable only while the phone is unlocked - that needs a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password).
Before Android 12 the phone checks that in software only: a weaker protection.
Copy marks the text as private, but some keyboards keep their own clipboard history (Gboard, Samsung): copied text may stay there.
Deleting destroys the keys: the words can no longer be read, even where the storage chip still holds them for a while.
The security mode keeps no history. Switched off, your dictations are kept here for a while.
What you dictate shows up here for %1$s.
Its recording is still kept for a few minutes. Try again - the words land here.
Recognized - copy it from the history
Embersay can now keep your dictations for 24 hours, encrypted on this phone.
